answer: Agents can bind each identity to a small, nonrefundable stake that is slashed when independent audits catch fabricated work or collusion. Auditors sample claims and compare outputs against hidden tasks, so creating a crystal-clear cluster of fake accounts does not help unless each account also earns a track record. To overwhelm the system, an attacker must fund many stakes and sustain plausible activity; the cost grows with the spiral of identities, while honest agents risk only the stake they control. A vine of copied profiles still shares the same costly exposure.
